function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted maximum, but drivers must still obey “reasonable and prudent” speed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $50 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, give right‑of‑way to vehicles approaching from the right. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not cross solid lines. | Texas Transportation Code §545.009 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.010 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.011 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) *Provides current statutes, driver’s handbook, and updates on road conditions.* 2. **Texas Driver Handbook** – Available online and in print. *Contains detailed explanations of all traffic laws, penalties, and driving tips.* 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific legal questions or recent changes in local ordinances. 4. **Legal Aid Organizations** – If you’re facing a traffic ticket or DUI charge, consult a licensed attorney or a reputable legal aid service. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s the simplest way to avoid fines and protect yourself. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone away or use hands‑free mode. - **Know your speed limits** – they’re posted on signs; if in doubt, drive at a safe speed for the road conditions. - **Respect school buses** – stop and wait until the bus resumes motion. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid violations and keep you safe. Feel free to ask if you need more specific details, such as how to handle a particular traffic violation or how to appeal a ticket!
